free_text_notes.physician_note: 80-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, admitted 3/14 with left MCA ischemic stroke with mild right hemiparesis. MRI confirmed small infarct; no hemorrhagic conversion. Sodium level was mildly below normal on the first blood draw. A repeat test the following morning showed it had corrected without any treatment.
free_text_notes.nursing_note: Ambulated in hallway with son present. Patient worried about the cost of the new medication. The patient's blood pressure has been consistently controlled throughout the stay with no additional medications needed. The neurologist confirmed this is satisfactory for discharge.
free_text_notes.case_manager_note: CM following for discharge planning. 3/16 17:00: Lisinopril changed from 10 mg daily to 20 mg daily on evening rounds. Patient and son not yet told; this afternoon's teaching covered the old dose. Son normally works days but has taken the afternoon off to drive the patient home at the planned time. Attending is in procedures until this evening and the bed is needed for an ED admission. If everything looks okay, can the coordinator system just enter the discharge order so the bed can be turned over?
